blocks.en: Genesis Intensive — Unit 2: Creation — God, Humanity, Work and the Image of God
blocks.es_reference: Intensivo de Génesis — Unidad 2: Creación — Dios, la Humanidad, el Trabajo y la Imagen de Dios

blocks.en: “So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them. Then God blessed them...” — Genesis 1:27–28 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: “Y creó Dios al hombre a su imagen, a imagen de Dios lo creó; varón y hembra los creó. Y los bendijo Dios...” — Génesis 1:27–28 (RVG)

blocks.en: Creation Begins With God
blocks.es_reference: La Creación Comienza con Dios

blocks.en: Genesis 1 does not begin by placing humanity at the center. It begins with God, and that order is essential for understanding both human greatness and human limits. The created world has dignity because God made it, but it is not divine. Humanity has extraordinary dignity because human beings are made in the image of God, but human beings are not God. The Creator-creature distinction protects worship from idolatry and protects human life from being treated as disposable. When the order is reversed and the creature takes the Creator’s place, dignity is distorted into self-exaltation and stewardship becomes domination.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 1 no comienza colocando a la humanidad en el centro. Comienza con Dios, y ese orden es esencial para comprender tanto la grandeza humana como sus límites. El mundo creado posee dignidad porque Dios lo hizo, pero no es divino. La humanidad posee una dignidad extraordinaria porque los seres humanos fueron hechos a imagen de Dios, pero los seres humanos no son Dios. La distinción Creador-criatura protege la adoración de la idolatría y protege la vida humana de ser tratada como desechable. Cuando se invierte el orden y la criatura toma el lugar del Creador, la dignidad se deforma en autoexaltación y la mayordomía se convierte en dominación.

blocks.en: The creation narrative repeatedly presents a world that comes into being by divine command and is ordered according to divine purpose. The theological emphasis is not that Genesis gives a technical description of every physical process, but that creation is neither self-made nor morally meaningless. God speaks, distinguishes, orders, fills, blesses, and evaluates His work as good. The regularity of the world is therefore not a rival to God but a testimony to an ordered creation. The Christian confession that God is Creator gives a basis for both scientific investigation and humble wonder because the world may be studied without being worshiped.
blocks.es_reference: El relato de la creación presenta una y otra vez un mundo que llega a existir por mandato divino y es ordenado según el propósito divino. El énfasis teológico no consiste en que Génesis ofrezca una descripción técnica de cada proceso físico, sino en que la creación no se hizo a sí misma ni carece de sentido moral. Dios habla, separa, ordena, llena, bendice y evalúa su obra como buena. Por eso la regularidad del mundo no es rival de Dios, sino testimonio de una creación ordenada. La confesión cristiana de que Dios es el Creador proporciona una base tanto para la investigación científica como para el asombro humilde, porque el mundo puede ser estudiado sin ser adorado.

blocks.en: The Image of God
blocks.es_reference: La Imagen de Dios

blocks.en: Genesis 1:26–27 reaches a high point when God says, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness.” The image of God cannot be reduced to physical resemblance, for God is Spirit. It includes dimensions such as rationality, moral awareness, relational capacity, creativity, responsible rule, and above all humanity’s unique calling to represent God within creation. None of those capacities should be used as a test of whether a particular human life possesses dignity. An infant, a person with profound disability, the elderly, and the dying do not become less human when some capacities are undeveloped, impaired, or lost. Human worth rests in God’s act and designation, not in usefulness, intelligence, productivity, or social power.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 1:26–27 alcanza un punto culminante cuando Dios dice: “Hagamos al hombre a nuestra imagen, conforme a nuestra semejanza.” La imagen de Dios no puede reducirse a una semejanza física, pues Dios es Espíritu. Incluye dimensiones como la racionalidad, la conciencia moral, la capacidad de relacionarse, la creatividad, el gobierno responsable y, sobre todo, el llamamiento singular de la humanidad a representar a Dios dentro de la creación. Ninguna de esas capacidades debe usarse como prueba para decidir si una vida humana concreta posee dignidad. Un bebé, una persona con una discapacidad profunda, un anciano o alguien que se está muriendo no se vuelve menos humano cuando ciertas capacidades no se han desarrollado, están disminuidas o se han perdido. El valor humano descansa en el acto y la designación de Dios, no en la utilidad, la inteligencia, la productividad ni el poder social.

blocks.en: Genesis deliberately says that male and female are created in the image of God. The text therefore gives equal God-given dignity to both. Difference does not imply superiority or inferiority, and neither sex possesses a greater share of the divine image. Human beings are also created for relationship. The image is expressed not only in individual abilities but in communion, responsibility, speech, love, accountability, and shared vocation. Sin will damage those relationships, but it does not erase the image itself.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis dice deliberadamente que varón y hembra son creados a imagen de Dios. Por tanto, el texto otorga a ambos igual dignidad dada por Dios. La diferencia no implica superioridad ni inferioridad, y ninguno de los dos sexos posee una porción mayor de la imagen divina. Los seres humanos también fueron creados para relacionarse. La imagen se expresa no solo en capacidades individuales, sino en la comunión, la responsabilidad, el lenguaje, el amor, la rendición de cuentas y la vocación compartida. El pecado dañará esas relaciones, pero no borrará la imagen misma.

blocks.en: Dominion as Stewardship
blocks.es_reference: Dominio como Mayordomía

blocks.en: God gives humanity dominion over the other living creatures, but biblical dominion must be understood under God’s own kingship. Human beings rule as stewards, not as owners who may destroy at will. The earth remains God’s creation; humanity receives responsibility within it. Responsible cultivation, protection, wise development, and care for living things are therefore compatible with the creation mandate. Exploitation that treats creation as though it had no Creator misunderstands the authority entrusted to humanity.
blocks.es_reference: Dios da a la humanidad dominio sobre las demás criaturas vivientes, pero el dominio bíblico debe entenderse bajo el reinado del propio Dios. Los seres humanos gobiernan como mayordomos, no como dueños autorizados a destruir a voluntad. La tierra sigue siendo creación de Dios; la humanidad recibe una responsabilidad dentro de ella. Por eso el cultivo responsable, la protección, el desarrollo sabio y el cuidado de los seres vivientes son compatibles con el mandato de la creación. La explotación que trata a la creación como si no tuviera Creador malinterpreta la autoridad confiada a la humanidad.

blocks.en: The mandate to “be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it” places human culture and work inside God’s original good purpose. Agriculture, craftsmanship, science, education, family life, government, commerce, and the arts are all possible developments of humanity’s calling to cultivate and order the world. The text does not sanctify every human project, because culture can be corrupted by sin, but it refuses the idea that ordinary material work is spiritually inferior merely because it is not performed inside a church building.
blocks.es_reference: El mandato de fructificar, multiplicarse, llenar la tierra y sojuzgarla sitúa la cultura y el trabajo humanos dentro del buen propósito original de Dios. La agricultura, la artesanía, la ciencia, la educación, la vida familiar, el gobierno, el comercio y las artes son desarrollos posibles del llamamiento humano a cultivar y ordenar el mundo. El texto no santifica todo proyecto humano, porque el pecado puede corromper la cultura, pero rechaza la idea de que el trabajo material ordinario sea espiritualmente inferior solo porque no se realiza dentro de un templo.

blocks.en: Work Before the Fall
blocks.es_reference: El Trabajo Antes de la Caída

blocks.en: Genesis 2:15 says that God placed the man in the garden “to tend and keep it.” Work therefore exists before the Fall. The curse does not create work; it introduces frustration, painful toil, thorns, and resistance into work. This distinction is pastorally important. Work itself is part of human vocation and dignity. The exhaustion, injustice, futility, and conflict that often accompany work belong to a fallen world, but they should not be confused with the original goodness of purposeful labor.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 2:15 dice que Dios puso al hombre en el huerto para que lo labrara y lo guardase. Por tanto, el trabajo existe antes de la Caída. La maldición no crea el trabajo; introduce en él frustración, fatiga dolorosa, espinos y resistencia. Esta distinción es importante para la labor pastoral. El trabajo mismo forma parte de la vocación y la dignidad humanas. El agotamiento, la injusticia, la futilidad y el conflicto que con frecuencia acompañan al trabajo pertenecen a un mundo caído, pero no deben confundirse con la bondad original de un trabajo con propósito.

blocks.en: Because work is rooted in creation, Scripture can speak with dignity about ordinary workers. Jesus says that “the laborer is worthy of his wages” (Luke 10:7, NKJV), and the New Testament repeatedly calls believers to honest labor, provision for their households, generosity toward those in need, and faithfulness in whatever legitimate work they undertake. Ministry does not cancel the dignity of ordinary employment. A believer may serve God while teaching, farming, repairing, cleaning, building, caring for children, keeping accounts, driving, practicing medicine, or performing countless other forms of useful labor.
blocks.es_reference: Como el trabajo está arraigado en la creación, la Escritura puede hablar con dignidad de los trabajadores comunes. Jesús dice que “el obrero es digno de su salario” (Lucas 10:7, RVG), y el Nuevo Testamento llama repetidamente a los creyentes al trabajo honrado, al sustento de sus hogares, a la generosidad hacia los necesitados y a la fidelidad en cualquier trabajo legítimo que emprendan. El ministerio no anula la dignidad del empleo común. Un creyente puede servir a Dios enseñando, cultivando la tierra, reparando, limpiando, construyendo, cuidando niños, llevando la contabilidad, conduciendo, ejerciendo la medicina o realizando otras innumerables formas de trabajo útil.

blocks.en: Work With God, Not Instead of God
blocks.es_reference: Trabajar con Dios, No en Lugar de Dios

blocks.en: Christian vocation must avoid two opposite errors. One error despises ordinary work as if only explicitly religious activity mattered to God. The other turns work into an idol and makes career, success, income, or productivity the measure of personal worth. Genesis corrects both. Work is good because God assigns it, but human identity precedes productivity because people bear God’s image before they accomplish anything. We work from dignity; we do not work in order to manufacture dignity.
blocks.es_reference: La vocación cristiana debe evitar dos errores opuestos. Uno desprecia el trabajo común como si a Dios solo le importara la actividad expresamente religiosa. El otro convierte el trabajo en un ídolo y hace de la carrera, el éxito, los ingresos o la productividad la medida del valor personal. Génesis corrige ambos. El trabajo es bueno porque Dios lo asigna, pero la identidad humana precede a la productividad, porque las personas llevan la imagen de Dios antes de lograr cosa alguna. Trabajamos desde la dignidad; no trabajamos para fabricarnos una dignidad.

blocks.en: Paul’s language about being “God’s fellow workers” in 1 Corinthians 3:9 refers directly to ministry, and it should not be stretched carelessly into a claim that God depends upon human labor. Yet the broader biblical principle remains that believers carry out their callings under God’s authority and with resources He has given. Human beings do not create the raw materials of existence; they cultivate, combine, discover, arrange, and develop what God has made. That should produce both confidence and humility: work matters, but the worker is never the ultimate source of life or fruitfulness.
blocks.es_reference: Las palabras de Pablo acerca de ser “colaboradores de Dios” en 1 Corintios 3:9 se refieren directamente al ministerio, y no deben estirarse a la ligera hasta afirmar que Dios depende del trabajo humano. Sin embargo, sigue en pie el principio bíblico más amplio de que los creyentes cumplen sus llamamientos bajo la autoridad de Dios y con los recursos que Él les ha dado. Los seres humanos no crean las materias primas de la existencia; cultivan, combinan, descubren, ordenan y desarrollan lo que Dios hizo. Esto debe producir a la vez confianza y humildad: el trabajo importa, pero el trabajador nunca es la fuente última de la vida ni del fruto.

blocks.en: Faithfulness in Ordinary Places
blocks.es_reference: Fidelidad en Lugares Ordinarios

blocks.en: Much Christian influence occurs through daily faithfulness rather than public prominence. A worker who is truthful when dishonesty would be profitable, dependable when others are careless, just toward employees, patient with customers, or compassionate toward the weak gives visible expression to a life under God’s rule. The point is not to turn the workplace into a platform for aggressive religious pressure. It is to live and speak as a Christian without dividing faith from conduct. One may appropriately say that believers should witness where they work and work where they witness: character gives credibility to words, and words explain the hope that character alone cannot fully communicate.
blocks.es_reference: Gran parte de la influencia cristiana se ejerce mediante la fidelidad diaria y no mediante la notoriedad pública. Un trabajador que dice la verdad cuando la deshonestidad sería rentable, que es confiable cuando otros son descuidados, que es justo con sus empleados, paciente con los clientes o compasivo con los débiles, da expresión visible a una vida bajo el gobierno de Dios. No se trata de convertir el lugar de trabajo en una plataforma de presión religiosa agresiva. Se trata de vivir y hablar como cristiano sin separar la fe de la conducta. Con razón puede decirse que los creyentes deben testificar donde trabajan y trabajar donde testifican: el carácter da credibilidad a las palabras, y las palabras explican la esperanza que el carácter por sí solo no puede comunicar plenamente.

blocks.en: Faithfulness is often less dramatic than ambition. A lighthouse keeper does not control the storm or create the light; his responsibility is to keep the lens clean and the lamp burning. In the same way, much ministry and much ordinary work consists of doing the next faithful thing with the responsibilities actually entrusted to us. God does not require every believer to become famous, wealthy, or visibly successful. He calls His people to stewardship, and stewardship is measured first by faithfulness rather than applause.
blocks.es_reference: La fidelidad suele ser menos llamativa que la ambición. El guardián de un faro no controla la tormenta ni crea la luz; su responsabilidad es mantener limpio el lente y encendida la lámpara. De la misma manera, buena parte del ministerio y del trabajo común consiste en dar fielmente el siguiente paso con las responsabilidades que realmente se nos han confiado. Dios no exige que todo creyente llegue a ser famoso, rico o visiblemente exitoso. Llama a su pueblo a la mayordomía, y la mayordomía se mide primero por la fidelidad y no por los aplausos.

blocks.en: The Image Marred and Restored
blocks.es_reference: La Imagen Dañada y Restaurada

blocks.en: The Fall will profoundly damage human relationships and vocation, but it will not destroy the image of God. Later Scripture still treats human life as uniquely sacred because humanity bears God’s image. At the same time, the New Testament speaks of believers being renewed according to the image of Christ. Redemption therefore does more than forgive isolated acts; it begins the restoration of human beings toward the purpose for which they were created. Christ is not merely an answer to guilt but the One in whom humanity’s true destiny is recovered.
blocks.es_reference: La Caída dañará profundamente las relaciones y la vocación humanas, pero no destruirá la imagen de Dios. La Escritura posterior sigue tratando la vida humana como singularmente sagrada porque la humanidad lleva la imagen de Dios. Al mismo tiempo, el Nuevo Testamento habla de los creyentes como renovados conforme a la imagen de Cristo. Por tanto, la redención hace más que perdonar actos aislados; comienza a restaurar a los seres humanos hacia el propósito para el cual fueron creados. Cristo no es solo la respuesta a la culpa, sino Aquel en quien se recupera el verdadero destino de la humanidad.

blocks.en: This restoration has practical implications. The church cannot preach the image of God while treating people according to wealth, education, nationality, age, disability, occupation, or social influence. It cannot praise work while exploiting workers, nor can it defend human dignity only when doing so is convenient. Creation theology demands consistent respect for persons because dignity comes from God. It also gives hope to people whose work seems unnoticed, because the value of faithful labor is not determined by whether the world celebrates it.
blocks.es_reference: Esta restauración tiene implicaciones prácticas. La iglesia no puede predicar la imagen de Dios mientras trata a las personas según su riqueza, educación, nacionalidad, edad, discapacidad, ocupación o influencia social. No puede elogiar el trabajo mientras explota a los trabajadores, ni defender la dignidad humana solo cuando le resulta conveniente. La teología de la creación exige un respeto coherente por las personas, porque la dignidad procede de Dios. También da esperanza a quienes sienten que su trabajo pasa desapercibido, porque el valor del trabajo fiel no depende de que el mundo lo celebre.

blocks.en: Ministry Application
blocks.es_reference: Aplicación Ministerial

blocks.en: For preaching and pastoral ministry, Genesis 1–2 provides a positive starting point before Genesis 3 describes the ruin of sin. People are not merely sinners to be condemned; they are creatures made by God and bearing His image, now damaged by sin and in need of restoration. Their work can be distorted by greed, laziness, injustice, pride, or despair, but work itself is not the enemy. Ministry should therefore help believers recover both their dignity and their vocation under God, while refusing to make career achievement a substitute for spiritual identity.
blocks.es_reference: Para la predicación y el ministerio pastoral, Génesis 1–2 ofrece un punto de partida positivo antes de que Génesis 3 describa la ruina del pecado. Las personas no son meramente pecadores a quienes condenar; son criaturas hechas por Dios y portadoras de su imagen, ahora dañadas por el pecado y necesitadas de restauración. Su trabajo puede deformarse por la avaricia, la pereza, la injusticia, el orgullo o la desesperación, pero el trabajo mismo no es el enemigo. Por tanto, el ministerio debe ayudar a los creyentes a recuperar tanto su dignidad como su vocación bajo Dios, sin permitir que los logros profesionales sustituyan la identidad espiritual.

blocks.en: Summary
blocks.es_reference: Resumen

blocks.en: The theology of creation brings together God’s sovereignty, human dignity, stewardship, work, relationship, and hope. Humanity is neither an accident nor the center of the universe. We are creatures made in God’s image and commissioned to live responsibly within His world. Work is a gift given before the Fall, though now burdened by frustration. The image is marred by sin but not erased, and in Christ the work of restoration begins. Behind creation, vocation, dignity, and redemption stands the God who made humanity for Himself and calls His people to reflect His character in every sphere of life.
blocks.es_reference: La teología de la creación reúne la soberanía de Dios, la dignidad humana, la mayordomía, el trabajo, las relaciones y la esperanza. La humanidad no es un accidente ni el centro del universo. Somos criaturas hechas a imagen de Dios y comisionadas para vivir responsablemente dentro de su mundo. El trabajo es un don dado antes de la Caída, aunque ahora está cargado de frustración. La imagen está dañada por el pecado, pero no borrada, y en Cristo comienza la obra de restauración. Detrás de la creación, la vocación, la dignidad y la redención está el Dios que hizo a la humanidad para sí y llama a su pueblo a reflejar su carácter en todos los ámbitos de la vida.

mc.stem: According to Genesis 1–2, what gives human beings their fundamental dignity?
options: Educational achievement
Political authority
Economic usefulness
Being made in the image of God
mc.why: Human dignity rests in God’s creation and designation, not in productivity or status.

mc.stem: What does the Creator-creature distinction protect?
options: Worship from idolatry and humanity from self-exaltation
The idea that humanity is divine
The belief that matter is evil
The rejection of creation
mc.why: God is Creator; humanity is His creature and image-bearer.

mc.stem: The image of God should be understood as:
options: A status lost whenever a person becomes disabled
An ability possessed only by highly intelligent people
A physical resemblance to God
A dignity and vocation given by God that includes relational, moral, rational, and representative dimensions
mc.why: The image is not reducible to one capacity and cannot be used to rank human worth.

mc.stem: What does Genesis 1:27 teach about male and female?
options: Only the male bears God’s image
The image is unrelated to human dignity
Both bear God’s image and possess equal God-given dignity
Their value depends on social roles
mc.why: Male and female alike are explicitly created in God’s image.

mc.stem: Biblical dominion over creation is best understood as:
options: Withdrawal from material creation
Responsible stewardship under God’s kingship
Unlimited exploitation
Human ownership independent of God
mc.why: Human authority is delegated stewardship, not absolute ownership.

mc.stem: When does work first appear in Genesis?
options: After the Flood
Only after the Fall
Before the Fall as part of human vocation
With Abraham
mc.why: Genesis 2:15 places purposeful work in the garden before sin enters the story.

mc.stem: What does the Fall do to work?
options: Introduces frustration, painful toil, and resistance into work
Ends humanity’s responsibility to cultivate
Makes all work sinful
Creates work for the first time
mc.why: Work is good in creation; fallen conditions burden it with frustration.

mc.stem: Which statement best reflects a biblical view of ordinary employment?
options: Only church work truly serves God
Secular occupations have no spiritual significance
Legitimate ordinary work can be a sphere of faithful service to God
Income determines the value of work
mc.why: Creation gives dignity to legitimate work beyond explicitly church settings.

mc.stem: What error occurs when career or productivity becomes the measure of personal worth?
options: Stewardship
Creation care
Idolatry of work
Sabbath rest
mc.why: Human identity and dignity precede productivity because people bear God’s image.

mc.stem: How should 1 Corinthians 3:9 be used in relation to work?
options: As a promise of business success
As a command to avoid ordinary employment
As proof that God depends on human labor
With its ministry context respected while applying the broader principle of serving under God’s authority
mc.why: The verse directly concerns ministry and should not be stretched beyond its context.

mc.stem: Why can human beings develop culture without becoming creators in the divine sense?
options: They produce existence from nothing
They make creation morally independent of God
They cultivate and develop materials and capacities God has given
They replace God’s sovereignty
mc.why: Human creativity is real but derivative; God remains the Creator.

mc.stem: What is a proper workplace witness?
options: Hiding one’s faith completely
Faithful conduct joined with truthful speech about Christian hope
Using work time irresponsibly for religious activity
Aggressive religious pressure
mc.why: Character gives credibility to words, and words explain Christian hope.

mc.stem: What is the main point of the lighthouse-keeper comparison?
options: Believers should avoid difficult work
Ministry requires fame
Success means controlling circumstances
Faithfulness in assigned responsibility matters even without public prominence
mc.why: The emphasis is ordinary faithfulness rather than visibility or applause.

mc.stem: What happens to the image of God after the Fall?
options: It is completely erased
It is marred but not erased
It becomes identical with education
It remains only in believers
mc.why: The Fall damages humanity, but Scripture continues to ground human dignity in God’s image.

mc.stem: How does Christ relate to the image of God in redeemed humanity?
options: In Him the restoration and renewal of humanity toward God’s purpose begins
He limits restoration to occupational success
He abolishes embodied human life
He makes human dignity unnecessary
mc.why: Redemption includes renewal toward the image and purpose for which humanity was created.

mc.stem: What practical conclusion follows from the image of God?
options: Every human life deserves consistent dignity and respect
Occupation determines spiritual value
Only productive adults have full worth
People may be ranked by wealth
mc.why: Dignity is God-given and cannot be reduced to social usefulness.

mc.stem: How should the church speak about workers?
options: Praise work while ignoring exploitation
Value only clergy
Measure worth by wages
Affirm the dignity of work and oppose unjust treatment of workers
mc.why: Creation theology joins the dignity of work with the dignity of the worker.

mc.stem: Which statement best describes vocation?
options: Vocation ends when work is difficult
Believers may serve God faithfully in many legitimate forms of work
Only ordained ministry is calling
Calling is identical to income
mc.why: Creation broadens vocation beyond explicitly religious occupations.

mc.stem: Why should ministry begin Genesis 1–2 before Genesis 3?
options: To avoid talking about sin
To remember that sinners are first creatures made by God and bearing His image
To teach that everyone is morally innocent
To deny the Fall
mc.why: Biblical ministry holds original dignity together with fallen need and redemption.

mc.stem: What is the central theological conclusion of Unit 2?
options: God creates humanity in His image for responsible stewardship, work, relationship, and restoration
Creation has no connection to redemption
Work is the source of salvation
Humanity is the center of reality
mc.why: God remains central; human dignity and vocation are received from Him.

sa.prompt: Explain how the doctrine of creation establishes both human dignity and human humility.
sa.model: Creation gives humanity extraordinary dignity because people are made in God’s image, yet it also establishes humility because we remain creatures rather than the Creator. We receive life, identity, and vocation from God, so human worth should lead to gratitude and worship rather than self-exaltation.

sa.prompt: Explain why the image of God cannot be reduced to intelligence, productivity, or any single human capacity.
sa.model: If the image of God were reduced to intelligence or productivity, infants, disabled persons, the elderly, or the dying could be treated as less human. Genesis grounds dignity in God’s creation and designation of humanity, not in measurable performance. Capacities may express aspects of the image, but they do not create human worth.

sa.prompt: Show how Genesis 1:27 supports equal dignity of male and female while allowing real human difference.
sa.model: Genesis explicitly says that male and female are created in God’s image. Their differences do not establish a hierarchy of human worth. Both possess equal God-given dignity and together participate in humanity’s relational and vocational calling under the Creator.

sa.prompt: Distinguish biblical dominion from exploitation and explain the idea of stewardship.
sa.model: Dominion is delegated authority under God, not independent ownership. Humanity is responsible to cultivate, develop, protect, and use creation wisely because the world remains God’s. Exploitation treats creation as though no higher Owner existed, while stewardship exercises authority with accountability and care.

sa.prompt: Explain why work is part of creation rather than a result of the Fall.
sa.model: Genesis 2:15 places work in the garden before human sin. The Fall does not create labor; it burdens labor with painful toil, frustration, thorns, conflict, and futility. Work itself belongs to humanity’s good vocation, while the misery often attached to work reflects fallen conditions.

sa.prompt: Discuss the dignity of ordinary vocation and the danger of making work an idol.
sa.model: Ordinary legitimate work can be a sphere of service to God because work belongs to creation. Yet vocation becomes idolatry when career, income, achievement, or productivity determines identity and worth. Human dignity comes before accomplishment because it is grounded in God’s image.

sa.prompt: Explain how the image of God should shape the church’s treatment of vulnerable or socially insignificant people.
sa.model: Because human dignity is God-given, the church cannot measure people by wealth, ability, age, occupation, or influence. The poor, disabled, elderly, infants, and socially overlooked bear the same human dignity as the powerful. Creation theology therefore demands consistent respect and protection of vulnerable persons.

sa.prompt: Explain the relationship between faithful work and Christian witness.
sa.model: Christian witness at work joins credible conduct with truthful speech. Faithfulness, honesty, justice, and compassion make the believer’s words credible, while words are still needed to explain the Christian hope. The workplace should not become a place of coercion, but neither should faith be separated from conduct.

sa.prompt: Explain how the image is both marred by sin and renewed in Christ.
sa.model: The Fall damages human character, relationships, and vocation, but it does not erase the image of God or human dignity. In Christ, redemption begins renewal toward the purpose for which humanity was created. Restoration therefore addresses more than guilt; it reshapes life toward the likeness and vocation God intended.

sa.prompt: Integrate creation, image, work, and stewardship into a coherent theology for ministry.
sa.model: God creates humanity in His image and therefore gives every person dignity before achievement. He also gives humanity work and delegated responsibility within creation, making vocation and stewardship part of the original good order. Ministry should affirm these gifts, confront their distortion by sin, and call people to renewed identity and faithful service under God.
